messages:
mike.h: heads up — noticed a weird spike in provisioning failures in eu-west1 gpu pool after last night's BIOS batch. nodes failing to come online, serial console times out :warning:
infra-bot: deploy-rollout started by @release-engineering: bios/2026-03-19-uefi-hotfix -> target: eu-west1 (60 hosts)
joe? we hit the same rollout, right?
sara: yes we did the rollout at 02:15 UTC, can confirm ~12/60 returned flaky consoles, but now it's growing to ~24. symptoms: IPMI responds but serial over LAN disconnects, and some nodes show SecureBoot toggled to Enabled when they were Disabled before. :eyes:
leo: quick check from jumpbox — running `efivar -l | grep -i SecureBoot` on one repro node shows `SecureBoot-00000001: 1`
leo: also seeing IPMI session counts spike, `ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.11.24.5 -U admin -P **** sel elist` times out a lot
tess: confirmed on monitoring — BMC session backlog at 95% on the affected rack. queueing/timeout causing provisioning orchestrator retries and double-spins. cost will spike if we keep retrying.
mike.h: ok pause the rollout? we should stop further hosts from getting the BIOS image until we understand the SecureBoot flip
sara: pausing now via release console, canaries held at 4 hosts.
ops-runbook: Runbook check: rollback path available — document `docs/runbooks/biOS-rollback.md`. Steps: 1) mark affected hosts drain 2) run remote BMC warm-reboot 3) reflash previous BIOS image 4) verify SecureBoot vars restored
leo: reproducer command I used: ```ssh jump@eu-west1-jump
# check uefi var
sudo efivar -l | grep -i SecureBoot
# check bmc sessions
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P $PASS chassis status
```
sara: pushing a small script to inspect multiple hosts: `parallel-ssh -h hosts.txt 'efivar -l | grep SecureBoot || echo no-efivar'` — running now, will post summary
mike.h: do we know which BIOS change toggled the var? release notes mention 'UEFI lockdown: enable TPM handling improvements' — could be a new vendor image defaulting SecureBoot=1
tess: vendor provided an updated image that inadvertently sets the SecureBoot variable during first boot. they scoped it to a specific microcode set. we're contacting them, but mitigation is local rollback or use vendor signoff to keep keys consistent.
leo: summary from parallel run: 24 hosts show SecureBoot=1, 36 show SecureBoot=0, 5 return no-efivar (BMC/console dead). list attached in thread (uploaded) :paperclip:
mike.h: plan A: rollback canary 4 hosts immediately, then roll forward rollback across affected hosts in rack groups. plan B: if BMC sessions unrecoverable, power-cycle via remote PDUs and force previous image through rescue mode.
sara: starting rollback on canary-1 (node eu1-gpu-023) — running `vendor-flash --image old-bios.bin --target /dev/mtd0 --force` now. monitor logs
leo: canary-1 reboots, serial shows pre-boot sequence, SecureBoot now 0. good sign :thumbsup:
tess: marking orchestration to stop retries for affected host set to avoid cost from provisioning churn. added backpressure rule: no >3 retries per host in 30m.
infra-bot: incident-created #INC-2026-0436: eu-west1 bios rollout causing BMC session backlog and SecureBoot toggles. priority: P2
mike.h: ok proceed with staged rollback. estimate 2.5h to clear backlog if no surprises. keep NOC posted
sara: quick note — cost impact: autoscaler triggered extra 20 preemptibles for retries in the last hour. finance FYI: spike ~0.6k USD if not contained. tagging @finance in incident thread.
leo: vendor replied: they say 'image sets SecureBoot to default enabled for newly provisioned systems' and sent a signed image that preserves the variable. we'll validate in a sandbox before reattempt.
ops-runbook: after rollback finished on rack A, run `efibootmgr -v` to ensure boot entries are intact and add monitoring alert for SecureBoot var flips
mike.h: update at +1h — rollback on first two racks done, BMC sessions back to normal for those. continuing with next batch.
sara: nice work, keep the pace but no more than 6 hosts concurrently to avoid spiking BMC sessions again.
leo: after-action item: add a preflight check to image deploy pipeline to detect changes to efivars. simple script run in serial console recovery mode should catch this.
mike.h: agree — creating ticket: INFRA-1347 preflight-check for efivars and BMC session threshold gating on rollouts
tess: adding retrospective note about vendor process to avoid defaulting SecureBoot on signed images.
mike.h: thanks all. will post final incident summary once all hosts cleared. :white_check_mark:
